## Breaking change

## Proposed change
- in core 0.105.5 marytts was changed to use WAVE_FILE for codec and language using underscores (en_us)
- this breaks the regex in tts and playing would fail
- this PR adjusts the filename and makes the regex include the new language identifier

I was going over the code. So I don't think we should change the regex. Normaly we map the data between interfaces like MaryTTS and our format. With this regex change, we end up with a hard to parse format.

Solution: `SUPPORT_LANGUAGES = MaryTTS.supported_locales()` loop over this and replace `_` with `-`.
We can also make sure that the component replaces `_` with `-` before we use the language options, so there is no change needed on marytts. Such PR would also be acceptable.
According to the git history of marytts, the change of "codec" causes this issue. So providing a mapping from mary supported codec to file extension should fix this.

issue_context.title: MaryTTS service no longer working after update to 0.105.5
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->
Calling the ```tts.marytts_say``` service causes an error and does not play the TTS file on a Sonos speaker after update to 0.105.5.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue: 0.105.5
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): 0.104.3
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Home Assistant Supervised on Ubuntu 18.04 host on a NUC
- Integration causing this issue: MaryTTS
- Link to integration documentation on our website:
 https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/marytts/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
tts:
  platform: marytts
  host: 172.17.0.2
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
2020-02-23 17:49:23 ERROR (SyncWorker_11) [homeassistant.components.sonos.media_player] Error on play_media with UPnP Error 714 received: Illegal MIME-Type from 192.168.0.125
```

## Additional information
Since updating from 0.104.3 to 0.105.5, using the tts.marytts_say service no longer works via dev tools services or in a script.  It was working fine previous to the upgrade.  I understand that there were breaking changes for MaryTTS in this release, but my config passes and TTS files are being generated.  I am using the following MaryTTS container installed in Docker (via the Portainer add-on):

 ```https://hub.docker.com/r/sliversniper/marytts```

I also tried installing and using a different container:

```https://hub.docker.com/r/synesthesiam/marytts```

and also not using the containers but installing the Hass.io add-on:

```https://github.com/Poeschl/Hassio-Addons``` (without the host line in the config)

but all three methods give the same issue.

I see that previous to the upgrade to 0.105, the files in the config/tts folder had the extension ```.wav```, for example

```5a9ec76875bd81ec09a927a8366597e16e3fa16c_en-us_-_marytts.wav```

but now they have the extension ```.wave_file```, for example

```a94a8fe5ccb19ba61c4c0873d391e987982fbbd3_en_us_12775392801011591206_marytts.wave_file```

I think this is probably the issue, and the media player cannot handle this file extension.  The Sonos is the only speaker I have available for use with a media player in HA, so I have not been able to test with something else.  I see someone has posted a somewhat similar issue here: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/issues/31854.  (Apologies if I should have added to that issue instead of creating this one - this is my first time submitting an issue to GitHub).

Just to note - Using the Hass.io add-on, if I go to the Demo-UI of MaryTTS via http://hassio-ipaddress:59125 and download the file that is created, it has the extension ``` .wav``` , not  ```.wave_file```.
comments:
This seems to be a problem with the tts component, probably when it tries to proxy the request to the generated file.  There's a [regexp in there](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/548838924400c447d4e50e30676cb6eb889dd94f/homeassistant/components/tts/__init__.py#L61) that no longer matches the generated file name.

It's used [here to deliver the file](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/548838924400c447d4e50e30676cb6eb889dd94f/homeassistant/components/tts/__init__.py#L427) and also elsewhere in the file when it's enumerating all of the relevant files.

I notice in the states developer tools a URL reference to the generated file in a `media_player` entity, and when I try to retrieve it, it get a 404 error.
was this ever resolved? I encounter the same problem in my setup

Investigating this a bit further, I thought could have fixed the problem in `mary_tts` with a change like this:
```
--- marytts/tts.py
+++ /config/custom_components/marytts/tts.py
@@ -86,4 +86,4 @@

         data = self._mary.speak(message, effects)

-        return self._mary.codec, data
+        return self._mary.codec.strip("_FILE"), data
```

Well, this fixes the extension of the file name to someting that's 3-4 characters long.  But I find that even doing this, that I get paths created in my `/config/tts` directory like:
```
ffe703a6f8241bff40dbd47904625b052d3f097c_en_us_11534912786698548096_marytts.wav
```
which are not going to match that regular expression in the `tts` component I referenced in a previous comment:
```
_RE_VOICE_FILE = re.compile(r"([a-f0-9]{40})_([^_]+)_([^_]+)_([a-z_]+)\.[a-z0-9]{3,4}")
```
That last component after `_en_us_` isn't going to match the `([a-z_]+)` part of the regular expression.  I haven't figured out how/what/who creates the actual path name in the `tts` component; I _don't think` the TTS provider does it..?

So, changing that regular expression in `homeassistant/components/tts/__init__.py` to:
```
_RE_VOICE_FILE = re.compile(r"([a-f0-9]{40})_([^_]+)_([^_]+)_([a-z0-9_]+)\.[a-z0-9]{3,4}")
```
along with that change to marytts to strip off the `_FILE` suffix seems to make it "work".   I'm uneasy as I don't really know how that pathname is fully generated and why that changed from the previously working version.

> I haven't figured out how/what/who creates the actual path name in the `tts` component; I _don't think` the TTS provider does it..?

This happens in the `homeassistant/components/tts/__init__.py`
```
key = KEY_PATTERN.format(msg_hash, language, options_key, engine).lower()
```
```
filename = f"{key}.{extension}".lower()
```
where `extension` is the `codec` in the MaryTTS settings, which is by default `WAVE_FILE`. Are you not cutting this to `.wave` instead of `.wav` in your example?

@oscaropenness at issue is that regexp.  The change I made in the `marytts` component to strip the extension down to something 3-4 characters long (in this case, "wav") wasn't sufficient.  

The problem was that the immediate preceeding pattern `_([a-z_]+)\.` stopped working because the key that was generated had digits in that part of the path name.

The pattern was 
```
_RE_VOICE_FILE = re.compile(r"([a-f0-9]{40})_([^_]+)_([^_]+)_([a-z_]+)\.[a-z0-9]{3,4}")
```
and I changed to to 
```
_RE_VOICE_FILE = re.compile(r"([a-f0-9]{40})_([^_]+)_([^_]+)_([a-z0-9_]+)\.[a-z0-9]{3,4}")
```
which made it "work".  But I'm still uneasy with this because I don't know why/how the key now has digits present.  It feels like that change addresses the observed symptom of the problem, but perhaps not the cause of why those digits starting to appear and if that's OK or not.

@lmamakos 
The filename has the following structure
```
HASHOFTHEMESSAGE_YOURLANGUAGE_HASHOFOPTIONS_TTSENGINE.CODEC
40digits_letterswithoutunderscore_9to10digits_wordwithletters.ususally3to4letters
```
I found [this tool](https://regex101.com/) helpful to see which part corresponds to which in the regex.

![Screenshot from 2020-04-08 07-57-30](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57111010/79831395-9a510700-83a7-11ea-8f43-707c02bd5927.jpg)

The addition of `0-9` results in the regex recognizing `HASHOFOPTIONS_TTSENGINE` together.
I think the main issue for you is that `([^_]+)` only recognizes the first part of your `en_us` because of the underscore.

Additionally the `.strip('_FILE')` is only working fine for the case of codec being `WAVE_FILE`. Since it will remove ALL occurrences of the letters, the setting `AIFF_FILE` would result in the extension `.A` which would not work.
To be generic we might need a different solution.
Something like
```
return self._mary.codec.replace('_FILE','').replace('WAVE','WAV'), data
```
could do the trick and would not interfere with other TTS engines since we only change `marytts`.

The regex might be a bit trickier, since it might break other TTS engines file patterns.
But I believe if we put the `([a-z0-9_-]+)` part at the end, we pretty much cover everything (I added the dash for potential TTS enginges beeing something like `amazing-tts`).
```
_RE_VOICE_FILE = re.compile(r"([a-f0-9]{40})_([^_]+)_([^_]+)_([a-z0-9_-]+)\.[a-z0-9]{3,4}")
```

Should I make a pull request with these two changes?

D'oh!  I must have spaced out and thought that `str.strip()` worked on the character string vs. each individual character; see what I get by doing premature optimization trying to avoid an anchored regexp or something?

I think that it's OK (at least it was when I tested) to have the entire `.WAVE` extensions; the tts regexp looks for a 3 to 4 character long match.  But it's probably more useful to convert to the more familiar `.WAV` suffix in any case.

Thanks for investigating this, I think a pull request with those changes would get marytts working again.
